page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.6xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by dedicated x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8163 processors clocked at 2.5 GHz. It provides 24 vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Vector extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside hardware-accelerated AES cryptography.

The instance is equipped with 48.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage is included, requiring all persistent disks to be network-attached. The platform features an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth allocation and does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses, nor does it include GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results reveal distinct performance tradeoffs between single-thread and parallel throughput. Single-threaded metrics, including stress-ng (1106.0), Geekbench single-core (991.0), and gzip compression (19.25 GB/sec), perform in the lower percentiles due to the conservative 2.5 GHz clock speed. Conversely, multi-threaded workloads show solid midrange capabilities, achieving 17696.41 in stress-ng multi-core, 7736.0 in Geekbench multi-core, and 18382.84 in the PassMark CPU evaluation. Memory throughput demonstrates stable performance, delivering 96.87 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 52.35 GB/sec for writes.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c5.6xlarge delivers scalable multi-core compute resources without the overhead of high memory ratios or bundled local storage. It is well-fitted for distributed batch processing, code compilation via toolchains such as Clang, static web serving (13.48 GB/sec throughput), and moderately sized in-memory caches like Redis, while remaining less suitable for latency-critical single-threaded execution or massive database workloads requiring local NVMe disks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.6xlarge is a compute-optimized x86_64 instance featuring 24 dedicated vCPUs (12 physical cores with hyper-threading) on Intel Xeon 8163 processors at 2.5 GHz. Configured with 48.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a compute-focused 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio alongside an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance bundles no local disk storage and lacks GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage. Benchmark testing indicates modest single-core throughput, reflected in weak single-thread Geekbench and compression scores, but solid midrange parallel execution, producing 17696.41 in multi-core stress-ng, 14250.0 in software compilation, and 16.98 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory bandwidth is stable, clocking 96.87 GB/sec for large uncached reads. This instance profile is engineered for parallel compute tasks, CI/CD compilation, web serving, and distributed processing environments requiring predictable multi-core density.
